sources.report:
About this data

These videos are previews rendered by OriginFlow: the egocentric camera with per-finger force traces (left and right hand), a hand-pose overlay, head and wrist trajectories, and an annotation timeline (episode, subtask, atomic action). The raw streams are not part of this folder, so the viewer shows the renders as delivered, downsampled from 120 to 30 fps.

Data quality, as reported by the provider

Frame-level validity flags over the OriginData preview dataset (10,867,077 frames). They count valid or detected frames; they do not measure force or pose accuracy.

FieldMeaningRate
left.force_validLeft-hand force values valid99.84%
right.force_validRight-hand force values valid99.84%
observation.hand.left.detectedLeft hand detected93.24%
observation.hand.right.detectedRight hand detected96.09%
observation.head.pose_validHead pose finite and aligned (not tracking quality)100.00%

Real-robot training results, as reported by the provider

Eight tasks trained from scratch (starVLA with a DiT-B head, batch 32; 641 sequences over 10 tasks, 525 train / 116 test): after 20,000 post-training steps the mean success rate was 34.35% with force input and 28.30% without. Squeezing salad dressing with 50,000 pretraining and 10,000 post-training steps: 75% (15/20) with force, 55% (11/20) without. Gains vary by task; stamping went from 15% without force to 10% with it.

sources.title: EgoTouch
sources.about: Bimanual tactile gloves with a chest camera and two fisheye wrist cameras, 213 everyday tasks.

hardware.d: Fingers, thumb and palm · shown on the release's 21×21 grid · 30 Hz
Plus WiLoR hand estimates in the release
The release also has a per-hand contact flag (not shown)

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2605.13083. The dataset card states no license; videos are played from the original repository, not copied.

sources.title: EgoTactile
sources.about: A right-hand pressure glove with a head- or neck-mounted egocentric camera, single grasps of 63 everyday objects by 12 participants, plus a bare-hand subset.

hardware.d: 4×3 fingertip pads, one strip per finger, 72-taxel palm · 0–350 N · about 17 Hz, held on a 15 Hz clock
Released at 1280×720 · 15 fps
Plus participant sex and hand length

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2606.09243 · project egotactile.github.io · code github.com/Russell-Zeng/EgoTactile. Videos are re-encoded to H.264 and redistributed under CC BY-NC 4.0 with attribution; the release ships MPEG-4 Part 2, which browsers cannot play. The glove model is not named in the paper. In the bare-hand subset the pressure comes from a synchronized off-camera gloved grasp.

sources.title: OpenTouch
sources.about: Egocentric in-the-wild recordings with a full-hand tactile glove on the right hand, Aria glasses video and Rokoko hand pose: 5.1 hours, 2,900 annotated clips in 14 environments.

hardware.d: 16×16 electrode grid, 169 taxels on fingers, thumb and palm (palmar side) · 30 Hz
RGB; 640×480 JPEG frames in the release · 30 fps · re-encoded here
21 hand landmarks + wrist and palm position · 30 Hz
Per clip, with contact onset, peak and post-contact frames

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2512.16842. The code repository's package metadata says MIT; the release states no license for the data, which is shared from Google Drive. The sample videos are re-hosted here for preview with attribution. Raw readings are 3072 at rest and fall with pressure; the viewer shows 3072 − raw, uncalibrated.

sources.title: HATO
sources.about: Teleoperated bimanual UR5e arms with two Psyonic Ability hands, six touch sites per fingertip; four tasks: banana handover, block stacking, wine pouring, steak serving.

hardware.d: 6 force-sensing sites per fingertip, 30 per hand · 12-bit ADC · logged at ≈10 Hz
Teleoperated with Meta Quest 2 controllers
One third-view, one on each wrist · 640×480

sources.notes: Paper: arXiv 2404.16823; code github.com/toruowo/hato; data on Berkeley Box (linked from the code README). The release states no license; the sample videos are re-hosted here for preview with attribution. Videos are built from the RGB frames stored in each step's pickle; depth is not shown. In the converted episodes the right hand's middle fingertip reads zero throughout, and some steps carry corrupted touch bytes (handled as described in each episode's notes). The wine-pouring task is not shown: every pour episode sampled had the right hand's touch bytes corrupted in most steps.
